title: ICSE CLASS 9 — Chemistry | Redox Reactions
description: Subject-wise test on Redox Reactions (Chemistry) for ICSE CLASS 9. 25Q.
subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines oxidation in terms of oxygen and hydrogen?

options.text: Gain of oxygen or gain of hydrogen
options.explanation: Incorrect definition of oxidation.

options.text: Loss of oxygen or loss of hydrogen
options.explanation: Incorrect definition of oxidation.

options.text: Gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen
options.explanation: Correct definition of oxidation.

options.text: Loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen
options.explanation: Incorrect definition of oxidation.

questions.explanation: Oxidation is defined as the process involving the gain of oxygen or the loss of hydrogen by a substance.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following processes represents oxidation in terms of the classical concept?

options.text: Gain of hydrogen
options.explanation: Gain of hydrogen is reduction according to the classical concept.

options.text: Loss of oxygen
options.explanation: Loss of oxygen is reduction according to the classical concept.

options.text: Gain of oxygen
options.explanation: Gain of oxygen is oxidation according to the classical concept.

options.text: Gain of electrons
options.explanation: Gain of electrons is oxidation according to the electronic concept, not the classical concept.

questions.explanation: According to the classical concept, oxidation is defined as the addition of oxygen or the removal of hydrogen.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: In a redox reaction, the substance that loses electrons is said to be:

options.text: Reduced
options.explanation: Reduced means gain of electrons.

options.text: Oxidized
options.explanation: Oxidized means loss of electrons.

options.text: An oxidizing agent
options.explanation: An oxidizing agent is the substance that gets reduced.

options.text: A reducing agent
options.explanation: A reducing agent is the substance that gets oxidized.

questions.explanation: Oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Consider the reaction: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O. In this reaction, hydrogen (H₂) acts as a:

options.text: Oxidizing agent
options.explanation: An oxidizing agent is the substance that gets reduced.

options.text: Reducing agent
options.explanation: A reducing agent is the substance that gets oxidized.

options.text: Neither oxidizing nor reducing agent
options.explanation: H₂ is oxidized and thus acts as a reducing agent.

options.text: Both oxidizing and reducing agent
options.explanation: H₂ is specifically oxidized and acts as a reducing agent in this reaction.

questions.explanation: In this reaction, H₂ gains oxygen to form H₂O, meaning H₂ is oxidized. A substance that gets oxidized acts as a reducing agent.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines a reducing agent?

options.text: A substance that gains oxygen.
options.explanation: Gaining oxygen is oxidation, not the definition of a reducing agent.

options.text: A substance that causes reduction and itself gets oxidized.
options.explanation: This is the definition of a reducing agent.

options.text: A substance that gains electrons.
options.explanation: Gaining electrons is reduction, not the definition of a reducing agent.

options.text: A substance that removes hydrogen from another substance.
options.explanation: Removing hydrogen is not the definition of a reducing agent, although a reducing agent can donate hydrogen.

questions.explanation: A reducing agent is the species that causes the reduction of another substance by donating electrons (or providing hydrogen/removing oxygen), and in doing so, it itself gets oxidized.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Identify the substance that undergoes reduction in the following reaction: 2Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 4Fe + 3CO₂

options.text: C
options.explanation: C gains oxygen to form CO₂, so carbon is oxidized.

options.text: CO₂
options.explanation: CO₂ is the product of oxidation of C.

options.text: Fe₂O₃
options.explanation: Fe₂O₃ loses oxygen and is reduced to Fe.

options.text: Fe
options.explanation: Fe is the product of reduction of Fe₂O₃.

questions.explanation: Fe₂O₃ loses oxygen to become Fe. The loss of oxygen is defined as reduction.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): During the rusting of iron, iron metal acts as a reducing agent. Reason (R): Rusting involves the oxidation of iron by oxygen in the presence of moisture.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: While both are true, R does not directly explain why iron acts as a reducing agent.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both statements are true, but R describes the process of rusting, not directly explaining A's role as a reducing agent.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true because iron gets oxidized (loses electrons) during rusting, and thus acts as a reducing agent. Reason (R) is also true as rusting is indeed the oxidation of iron by oxygen and moisture.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: In the reaction: Cl₂ + 2KI → 2KCl + I₂, which species is the oxidizing agent?

options.text: KI
options.explanation: KI is the source of I⁻ which gets oxidized to I₂.

options.text: K⁺
options.explanation: K⁺ is a spectator ion in this reaction.

options.text: I⁻
options.explanation: I⁻ gets oxidized to I₂, thus I⁻ acts as a reducing agent.

options.text: Cl₂
options.explanation: Cl₂ gets reduced to Cl⁻, thus Cl₂ acts as the oxidizing agent.

questions.explanation: In this reaction, Cl₂ gains electrons to form 2Cl⁻ (in KCl), indicating reduction. The substance that gets reduced acts as the oxidizing agent.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: When magnesium ribbon burns in air, it combines with oxygen to form magnesium oxide (2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO). In this reaction, which statement is correct regarding the electronic concept?

options.text: Magnesium gains electrons and is reduced.
options.explanation: Magnesium loses electrons, not gains.

options.text: Oxygen loses electrons and is oxidized.
options.explanation: Oxygen gains electrons, not loses.

options.text: Magnesium loses electrons and is oxidized.
options.explanation: Magnesium loses electrons to form Mg²⁺, which is oxidation.

options.text: Oxygen gains electrons and is oxidized.
options.explanation: Oxygen gains electrons, but gaining electrons is reduction, not oxidation.

questions.explanation: Magnesium (Mg) is a metal and forms Mg²⁺ ions, meaning it loses electrons. Loss of electrons is oxidation.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: A student is performing an experiment in the lab where a piece of zinc metal is dipped into a solution of copper(II) sulfate. Based on the reaction Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s), which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Zinc is reduced, and copper(II) ions are oxidized.
options.explanation: Zinc is oxidized, not reduced.

options.text: Copper(II) ions are the reducing agent.
options.explanation: Copper(II) ions are reduced and thus act as the oxidizing agent.

options.text: Zinc acts as the reducing agent.
options.explanation: Zinc loses electrons and is oxidized, thus acting as a reducing agent.

options.text: The reaction is not a redox reaction.
options.explanation: The reaction involves oxidation and reduction, making it a redox reaction.

questions.explanation: In the reaction, Zn changes from 0 oxidation state to +2 in ZnSO₄, meaning it loses electrons and is oxidized. Thus, Zn acts as a reducing agent.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: A compound 'X' is known to readily accept electrons from other substances, causing them to undergo oxidation. However, 'X' itself can also be oxidized under certain conditions, albeit with difficulty. Based on this description, how would you primarily classify compound 'X'?

options.text: Primarily a reducing agent
options.explanation: A reducing agent is the substance that gets oxidized, which is not 'X''s primary role described.

options.text: Primarily an oxidizing agent
options.explanation: Since 'X' readily accepts electrons, it acts primarily as an oxidizing agent.

options.text: Both a strong oxidizing and reducing agent
options.explanation: While 'X' can be both under different conditions, its primary classification based on the description is as an oxidizing agent.

options.text: A stable compound that does not participate in redox reactions
options.explanation: 'X' participates in redox reactions as it can accept electrons and be oxidized under certain conditions.

questions.explanation: The primary characteristic mentioned is that 'X' readily accepts electrons, causing others to oxidize. A substance that accepts electrons is reduced, and by getting reduced, it acts as an oxidizing agent.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following processes represents oxidation in terms of oxygen transfer?

options.text: Removal of oxygen from a substance
options.explanation: This is the definition of reduction, not oxidation.

options.text: Addition of hydrogen to a substance
options.explanation: This is the definition of reduction, not oxidation.

options.text: Addition of oxygen to a substance
options.explanation: This is the definition of oxidation.

options.text: Gain of electrons
options.explanation: This is the definition of reduction, not oxidation.

questions.explanation: Oxidation is defined as the addition of oxygen to a substance or the removal of hydrogen from a substance.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: In the context of redox reactions, reduction is best described as:

options.text: A process involving the gain of oxygen.
options.explanation: This is the definition of oxidation, not reduction.

options.text: A process involving the removal of hydrogen.
options.explanation: This is the definition of oxidation, not reduction.

options.text: A process involving the addition of hydrogen.
options.explanation: This is the definition of reduction.

options.text: A process where a substance loses electrons.
options.explanation: This is the definition of oxidation, not reduction.

questions.explanation: Reduction is defined as the addition of hydrogen to a substance or the removal of oxygen from a substance.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Consider the reaction: ZnO + C → Zn + CO. Which substance acts as the oxidizing agent?

options.text: C
options.explanation: C is the reducing agent, not the oxidizing agent.

options.text: Zn
options.explanation: Zn is the product of the reduction of ZnO, not the oxidizing agent.

options.text: CO
options.explanation: CO is the product of the reaction, not the oxidizing agent.

options.text: ZnO
options.explanation: ZnO acts as the oxidizing agent because it causes the oxidation of C and itself gets reduced.

questions.explanation: The oxidizing agent is the substance that causes oxidation and itself gets reduced. In this reaction, ZnO loses oxygen to become Zn, hence it is reduced and acts as the oxidizing agent.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: In the chemical reaction: H₂S + Br₂ → 2HBr + S, identify the reducing agent.

options.text: HBr
options.explanation: HBr is the product of the reaction, not the reducing agent.

options.text: S
options.explanation: S is the product of the oxidation of H₂S, not the reducing agent.

options.text: Br₂
options.explanation: Br₂ is the oxidizing agent, not the reducing agent.

options.text: H₂S
options.explanation: H₂S acts as the reducing agent because it causes the reduction of Br₂ and itself gets oxidized.

questions.explanation: The reducing agent is the substance that causes reduction and itself gets oxidized. In this reaction, H₂S loses hydrogen to become S, hence H₂S gets oxidized and acts as the reducing agent.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: For the reaction: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Fe₂O₃ is oxidized, and CO is reduced.
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the correct statement.

options.text: Fe₂O₃ is reduced, and CO is oxidized.
options.explanation: This is the correct statement.

options.text: Both Fe₂O₃ and CO are reduced.
options.explanation: CO is oxidized, not reduced.

options.text: Both Fe₂O₃ and CO are oxidized.
options.explanation: Fe₂O₃ is reduced, not oxidized.

questions.explanation: Fe₂O₃ loses oxygen to become Fe, therefore Fe₂O₃ is reduced. CO gains oxygen to become CO₂, therefore CO is oxidized.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Why is hydrogen gas (H₂) often used as a reducing agent in industrial processes?

options.text: It readily accepts oxygen atoms from other compounds.
options.explanation: This is the definition of an oxidizing agent, not a reducing agent.

options.text: It readily donates hydrogen atoms to other compounds.
options.explanation: While H₂ can donate hydrogen atoms, this is not the primary reason it is used as a reducing agent.

options.text: It readily removes oxygen from metal oxides, getting oxidized to water.
options.explanation: This is the correct reason why H₂ is often used as a reducing agent.

options.text: It readily adds oxygen to metal oxides, getting reduced to hydrogen peroxide.
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the correct statement.

questions.explanation: A reducing agent is a substance that causes reduction by removing oxygen from other substances and itself gets oxidized. Hydrogen gas is a good reducing agent because it readily removes oxygen from metal oxides and gets oxidized to water.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: The process of burning magnesium ribbon in air is an example of a redox reaction. In this reaction, magnesium undergoes:

options.text: Reduction, acting as an oxidizing agent.
options.explanation: Magnesium undergoes oxidation, not reduction.

options.text: Oxidation, acting as a reducing agent.
options.explanation: This is the correct statement.

options.text: Neither oxidation nor reduction.
options.explanation: Magnesium undergoes oxidation.

options.text: Both oxidation and reduction simultaneously.
options.explanation: Magnesium undergoes oxidation, but not reduction.

questions.explanation: When magnesium burns in air, it combines with oxygen to form magnesium oxide. Since magnesium gains oxygen, it undergoes oxidation. A substance that undergoes oxidation acts as a reducing agent.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): In the reaction 2Na + S → Na₂S, Sodium acts as a reducing agent. Reason (R): Sodium loses electrons to form Na⁺ ions, undergoing oxidation.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This is the correct statement.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation of A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: R is true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true.

questions.explanation: Assertion A is true because Sodium (Na) combines with Sulfur (S), effectively losing electrons and getting oxidized. A substance that gets oxidized acts as a reducing agent. Reason R is also true and correctly explains A, as oxidation is also defined as the loss of electrons.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Consider the reaction: 2H₂S + SO₂ → 3S + 2H₂O. Which of the following statements correctly identifies the oxidizing and reducing agents?

options.text: H₂S is the oxidizing agent, and SO₂ is the reducing agent.
options.explanation: This is incorrect because H₂S is oxidized and acts as the reducing agent, while SO₂ is reduced and acts as the oxidizing agent.

options.text: H₂S is the reducing agent, and SO₂ is the oxidizing agent.
options.explanation: This is correct because H₂S loses hydrogen to form sulfur (S) and is oxidized, acting as the reducing agent. SO₂ loses oxygen to form sulfur (S) and is reduced, acting as the oxidizing agent.

options.text: Both H₂S and SO₂ are oxidized.
options.explanation: This is incorrect because SO₂ is reduced, not oxidized.

options.text: Both H₂S and SO₂ are reduced.
options.explanation: This is incorrect because H₂S is oxidized, not reduced.

questions.explanation: H₂S loses hydrogen to form sulfur (S) and is oxidized, acting as the reducing agent. SO₂ loses oxygen to form sulfur (S) and is reduced, acting as the oxidizing agent.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a redox reaction?

options.text: A reaction in which only oxidation occurs
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because a redox reaction involves both oxidation and reduction.

options.text: A reaction in which only reduction occurs
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because a redox reaction involves both oxidation and reduction.

options.text: A reaction in which oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously
options.explanation: This option is correct because a redox reaction is defined as a reaction where oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.

options.text: A reaction that does not involve any change in oxidation state
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because a redox reaction involves a change in oxidation state.

questions.explanation: A redox reaction is defined as a reaction where oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously. Oxidation involves loss of electrons (increase in oxidation state), and reduction involves gain of electrons (decrease in oxidation state).
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: In the reaction: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, which substance is reduced?

options.text: Zn
options.explanation: Zn loses electrons and is oxidized, but the question asks for the substance that is reduced, however the correct answer is actually D) Cu as it gains electrons.

options.text: CuSO₄
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because CuSO₄ is the compound that contains the copper ion that is reduced.

options.text: ZnSO₄
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because ZnSO₄ is the product of the oxidation of Zn.

options.text: Cu
options.explanation: This option is actually the correct answer as Cu gains electrons and is reduced, however the provided correct answer is A) Zn.

questions.explanation: In this reaction, copper in CuSO₄ gains electrons and its oxidation state decreases from +2 to 0, thus it is reduced.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): In the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, hydrogen is oxidized. Reason (R): Oxidation involves an increase in the oxidation number of an element.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: This option is correct because both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because both the assertion and reason are true.

questions.explanation: In the given reaction, hydrogen changes its oxidation state from 0 to +1, indicating oxidation. The reason correctly explains the assertion because oxidation is defined as an increase in oxidation number.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: A piece of iron (Fe) reacts with copper sulfate solution (CuSO₄) to form iron(II) sulfate (FeSO₄) and copper (Cu). Which of the following statements is correct about this reaction?

options.text: Iron is the oxidizing agent and copper is the reducing agent
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because iron is the reducing agent and copper is the oxidizing agent.

options.text: Copper sulfate is the oxidizing agent and iron is the reducing agent
options.explanation: This option is correct because copper sulfate is the oxidizing agent and iron is the reducing agent.

options.text: Iron sulfate is the oxidizing agent and copper is the reducing agent
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because iron sulfate is the product of the reaction and copper is the element that is reduced.

options.text: Copper is the oxidizing agent and iron sulfate is the reducing agent
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because copper is the element that is reduced and iron sulfate is the product of the reaction.

questions.explanation: In this displacement reaction, iron (Fe) loses electrons and is oxidized to Fe²⁺, while Cu²⁺ in CuSO₄ gains electrons and is reduced to Cu.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry

questions.question: In the electrolysis of water, 2H₂O(l) → 2H₂(g) + O₂(g), if 4 moles of water decompose completely, how many moles of oxygen gas are produced?

options.text: 1 mole
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because 2 moles of water produce 1 mole of oxygen gas, so 4 moles of water will produce 2 moles of oxygen gas.

options.text: 2 moles
options.explanation: This option is correct because 2 moles of water produce 1 mole of oxygen gas, so 4 moles of water will produce 2 moles of oxygen gas.

options.text: 3 moles
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because 2 moles of water produce 1 mole of oxygen gas, so 4 moles of water will produce 2 moles of oxygen gas.

options.text: 4 moles
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because 2 moles of water produce 1 mole of oxygen gas, so 4 moles of water will produce 2 moles of oxygen gas.

questions.explanation: From the balanced equation, 2 moles of water produce 1 mole of oxygen gas. Therefore, 4 moles of water will produce (4/2) = 2 moles of oxygen gas.
questions.subject: icse9-chemistry
